questions.a: Oral cancer is a malignant tumor that develops in the tissues of the mouth or throat. It can affect the lips, inner cheeks, gums, tongue, or deeper areas. Early detection significantly improves treatment outcomes.
Over 54,000 people are diagnosed with oral cancer annually in the US. However, early detection has improved survival rates from 50% to over 90% when caught in early stages.

questions.q: Is early detection oral cancer curable?
questions.a: Yes! When oral cancer is detected early (Stage 1-2), the 5-year survival rate is over 80-90%. This is why early detection through regular screenings is crucial.
Stage 1: ~80-90% | Stage 2: ~70-80% | Stage 3: ~50-60% | Stage 4: ~20-40%. Early detection makes a critical difference!

ONCOAi uses a deep learning model trained on thousands of oral images. While highly accurate (94%+ in testing), it's a screening tool - not a replacement for professional diagnosis. Always consult a doctor.

questions.q: What does the confidence score mean?
questions.a: The confidence score (0-100%) indicates how certain the AI is about its prediction. Higher confidence means the model is more sure. A 95% CANCER confidence means high likelihood, but medical confirmation is essential.
Yes, like any diagnostic tool, false positives and false negatives are possible. The AI may flag benign conditions as concerning. Always consult a healthcare professional for confirmation.
Upload clear, well-lit photos of the affected area. Avoid blurry, dark, or heavily shadowed images. Multiple angles help improve accuracy.

questions.q: Is my data private and secure?
questions.a: Your uploaded images and data are handled securely per our privacy policy. We don't share personal data with third parties. Check our complete privacy policy for details.

questions.q: What should I do if ONCOAi shows CANCER?
questions.a:
1) Don't panic - it requires medical confirmation
2) Schedule an urgent appointment with an oral specialist or dentist
3) Bring the image and ONCOAi result
4) Get a professional biopsy if recommended
5) Follow medical advice for further testing

questions.q: What if the result is SUSPICIOUS?
questions.a: Schedule an appointment with your dentist or doctor within 1-2 weeks. SUSPICIOUS means the AI detected features that warrant professional evaluation. It doesn't mean cancer, but professional confirmation is needed.

questions.q: What is a biopsy and does it hurt?
questions.a: A biopsy is a tissue sample taken for microscopic examination - the gold standard for cancer diagnosis. Local anesthesia is used, so pain is minimal. Results take 1-2 weeks.

questions.q: What are oral cancer treatment options?
questions.a: Common treatments include: Surgery (tumor removal), Radiation therapy, Chemotherapy, or combination therapy. Treatment depends on cancer stage, type, and patient factors. Discuss with your oncologist.

questions.q: How can I prevent oral cancer?
questions.a:
✓ Quit tobacco (smoking, chewing)
✓ Limit alcohol consumption
✓ Maintain good oral hygiene
✓ Use SPF lip balm outdoors
✓ Eat a diet rich in fruits & vegetables
✓ Get regular dental checkups
✓ Avoid HPV infection (vaccination)

questions.q: Can HPV vaccine prevent oral cancer?
questions.a: Yes! HPV vaccination (Gardasil, Cervarix) prevents infection with high-risk HPV strains. It's most effective before sexual debut, but can benefit adults up to age 45. Consult your doctor.

questions.q: How often should I get dental checkups?
questions.a: General recommendation: Every 6 months for routine check-ups. Higher-risk individuals should see a dentist every 3 months. Include oral cancer screening in your visits.

questions.q: How do I do oral self-examination?
questions.a:
Monthly check:
1) Look in mirror under good light
2) Check lips, inner cheeks, gums, tongue
3) Feel for lumps or roughness
4) Note any white/red patches
5) Report changes to your dentist
Use ONCOAi if you notice changes!
